title: Detect actionable coronary plaque risk before a first clinical event

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a practical, affordable, noninvasive way to identify people whose coronary plaque places them at actionable risk before their first clinical event. Actionable risk means that the result supports a preventive treatment decision that improves outcomes. The intended capability combines risk detection, estimation of a person's likelihood of an event over a defined period, and evidence that acting on the result benefits that person.

As a synthesis of the supplied concept, the central goal is to connect plaque information to person-level prevention. A clinically useful test would identify otherwise unrecognized risk and help determine who benefits from additional prevention beyond existing assessment. Its success would depend on the complete pathway from testing through treatment and follow-up.

significance.text: If accurate detection led to effective preventive treatment, this capability could substantially improve primary prevention of heart attacks. Its direct value would be better treatment decisions and fewer first events among people whose actionable risk would otherwise go unrecognized. Affordability and applicability across diverse populations would determine how widely those benefits could extend. These are conditional benefits of the proposed innovation.

A further possibility is more selective use of preventive resources, with additional treatment directed toward people likely to benefit. That possibility depends on comparative clinical evidence. False-positive results, missed events, treatment harms and unnecessary procedures could offset gains. Detection alone cannot establish prevention benefit, and identifying a suspicious lesion cannot establish that treating that lesion will improve a person's overall outcome.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is reliable identification of coronary plaque risk that changes preventive decisions early enough to improve first-event outcomes. The supplied research identifies several proposed biological obstacles: plaque characteristics and risk may change over time, many suspicious plaques may never cause an event, and events may arise from lesions that were not identified beforehand. These natural-history assertions remain unverified in the supplied evidence because the retained source contains no scientific content.

As an engineering and clinical synthesis, the test would need to translate a noninvasive measurement into a calibrated estimate of future risk over a specified time horizon. It would also need to add decision-relevant information beyond existing assessment. The development problem includes measurement reliability, performance across patient groups, interpretation of uncertain results, and a workable testing and follow-up burden.

A separate unresolved requirement is demonstrating that the treatment pathway triggered by the test produces net benefit. Even a reproducible association between a plaque feature and subsequent events leaves open which patients should receive additional treatment, which intervention helps, and whether treatment gains exceed the consequences of testing and intervention. This distinction between predictive performance and clinical utility is part of the proposed breakthrough.

current_state.text: The supplied research identifies PREVENT, attributed to Seung-Jung Park and colleagues and dated 8 April 2024 in The Lancet, as a relevant clinical study. It describes selected patients undergoing intracoronary identification of high-risk plaques and comparison of preventive percutaneous coronary intervention with optimal medical therapy alone. According to that research summary, preventive intervention reduced a composite of target-vessel outcomes that included revascularization and hospitalization. These study details are retained as reported findings from the supplied research, with verification limited by the source-access failure described below.

The validated review found that the retained source artifact contained only a cookie-access message. It could not confirm the article's identity from document content or inspect its abstract, methods, population, endpoints or results. Although the source index records a saved artifact, that record does not resolve the lack of scientific text. The supplied materials provide no inspectable numerical effect estimate. This access limitation leaves the reported findings unverified here and provides no evidence that they are false.

On the supplied research's description, PREVENT concerns invasive assessment and treatment of selected lesions. Establishing that a noninvasive screening strategy prevents first heart attacks in initially asymptomatic populations would require additional evidence about that screening pathway and its outcomes. Likewise, a reduction in a composite containing hospitalization and revascularization would require examination of its individual components before drawing conclusions about heart-attack prevention. The absent study text prevents checking those distinctions against PREVENT's actual data.

The supplied search record is empty. Consequently, the materials do not establish the field's status as of the review's 1 November 2026 reference date or identify subsequent advances. The proposal's affordability, population applicability and first-event prevention benefit remain capabilities to demonstrate within this record.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration criteria begin with prospective validation of a practical noninvasive test in diverse, initially asymptomatic populations. Studies should specify the intended population, prediction horizon, clinical action and comparator. They should report calibration, absolute event risk, missed events and false positives, together with the incremental contribution beyond existing risk assessment. No single accuracy threshold is adopted because one aggregate accuracy figure would leave important questions about risk estimation and clinical utility unanswered.
completion_criteria.label: Prospective validation of noninvasive risk prediction in diverse asymptomatic populations

completion_criteria.text: A proposed decisive clinical demonstration would be a randomized comparison of a test-guided prevention strategy with current prevention, showing fewer first heart attacks and overall net benefit. Studies should report heart attacks separately from revascularization, hospitalization and other composite components, so that the outcome supporting the claim is clear. Treatment harms and additional procedures should be included in the benefit–harm assessment.
completion_criteria.label: Randomized test-guided prevention reduces first heart attacks with net benefit

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical criteria include independent validation across sites and relevant patient groups, reliable measurements in routine use, and transparent reporting of inconclusive results. Evaluation should establish affordability, access, follow-up requirements and the boundaries within which testing remains beneficial. These are proposed demonstrations for this innovation. Successful finite studies would establish the populations, settings and time horizons tested, with further evidence needed for broader application.
completion_criteria.label: Independent validation establishes reliable, affordable testing within stated benefit boundaries

related_concepts.text: CAR-02, “Reliably reverse advanced atherosclerosis throughout the arterial tree,” overlaps through its focus on atherosclerotic disease. Based on the supplied roster title, CAR-02 seeks a systemic therapeutic capability, while CAR-12 seeks early risk identification linked to preventive decisions. A successful reversal therapy could potentially be part of a test-guided prevention pathway, but each concept has its own completion requirements.

CAR-06, “Make most preventable sudden cardiac deaths predictable and preventable,” overlaps in the ambition to anticipate serious events and enable intervention. Its stated outcome is broader than coronary plaque risk. CAR-12 focuses on actionable coronary risk before a first clinical event, and its proposed heart-attack prevention demonstration would establish only the portion of CAR-06's ambition directly evaluated. This comparison rests on the supplied roster titles because detailed CAR-02 and CAR-06 records were not provided.

CAR-01, “Regenerate a severely damaged adult human heart,” provides a further conceptual connection through the consequences of cardiac injury. Successful first-event prevention could conditionally reduce some future need for repair, while CAR-01 addresses regeneration after severe damage. This relationship is a synthesis from the roster titles, with no supplied evidence quantifying the downstream effect.

unresolved_issues: PREVENT's bibliographic identity, study population, endpoint definitions, numerical results and individual outcome components remain unverified from the retained artifact.
The biological assertions about changing plaque risk, suspicious plaques that never cause events and events from previously unidentified lesions need inspectable supporting evidence.
The empty search record leaves the field's status as of 1 November 2026 unassessed.
The intended prediction horizon, test modality, treatment rules and acceptable benefit–harm trade-offs remain unspecified.
Affordability, population applicability and net benefit from noninvasive first-event screening are proposed capabilities whose achievement is not established by the supplied evidence.
Detailed CAR-02 and CAR-06 materials would be needed to verify their scope beyond the supplied roster titles.

brief.title: Finding hidden heart attack risk in time to act
possible: People without symptoms could learn whether plaque—fatty deposits in the arteries supplying the heart—puts them at risk that warrants extra preventive treatment. A practical, affordable test would work without entering an artery and connect the result to treatment proven to help.
why: This could prevent first heart attacks among people whose danger otherwise goes unnoticed. It would give patients and doctors a better basis for deciding who needs additional prevention.
Preventive care could reach more people who stand to benefit. Affordable testing that works across different populations would help those benefits extend widely.

sources.who: Seung-Jung Park and the PREVENT investigators
sources.showed: In selected patients, an invasive procedure to treat high-risk plaque reduced a combined measure of cardiac problems compared with medicines alone. That measure included hospital admissions and further artery procedures.
sources.quote: In patients with non-flow-limiting vulnerable coronary plaques, preventive percutaneous coronary intervention reduced major adverse cardiac events arising from high-risk vulnerable plaques, compared with optimal medical therapy alone.
sources.cited_for: Treating selected high-risk plaques can improve a combined measure of cardiac outcomes.
sources.not_established: This does not establish that screening people without symptoms prevents first heart attacks.

sources.showed: The team studied automated measurement of plaque and artery narrowing on heart scans, alongside heart attack risk prediction. Measurements were highly repeatable in a subset.
sources.cited_for: Automated scan analysis offers progress toward repeatable plaque measurement and risk assessment.
sources.not_established: Repeatable measurements do not establish that decisions based on the test improve health.

shown: Park and colleagues have connected invasive plaque assessment and treatment to better combined cardiac outcomes in selected patients. Lin and colleagues have studied automated plaque measurement and risk prediction from scans. These are parts of the pathway from detecting risk to preventing an event.
missing: A practical test must predict future events reliably in diverse people without symptoms and improve on existing risk assessment.
A trial must establish that prevention guided by the test reduces first heart attacks, with benefits exceeding treatment harms and extra procedures.
Independent studies must establish reliable routine use, affordability, access and manageable follow-up.

milestones.label: Reliable risk prediction in people without symptoms
milestones.explanation: Studies following diverse people without symptoms would have to show accurate risk estimates over a stated period, beyond existing assessment. This would establish whether the test adds useful information for prevention.

milestones.label: Fewer first heart attacks with overall benefit
milestones.explanation: A randomized trial would have to show fewer first heart attacks with test-guided prevention than with current care, counting harms and extra procedures. This would establish that acting on the result helps patients.

milestones.label: Reliable, affordable testing with clear limits
milestones.explanation: Independent studies would have to establish reliable, affordable testing across sites and patient groups, including unclear results and follow-up needs. This would define where testing remains beneficial in routine care.

uncertain: The prediction period, choice of test and treatment rules remain unspecified.
The acceptable balance between prevented heart attacks, false alarms, missed events and treatment harms remains open.

page.title: Coronary CT angiography–guided primary prevention
page.definition: Coronary CT angiography is a noninvasive X-ray scan that shows plaque in the arteries supplying the heart. SCOT-HEART 2 tests whether using the scan to guide preventive treatment in asymptomatic adults aged 40–70 with cardiovascular risk factors and no known cardiovascular disease reduces coronary heart disease death or first nonfatal heart attack compared with care guided by a 10-year risk score.

goal.need: US data from 2005–2014 put the annual number of first heart attacks at 605,000. A risk score estimates a person's chance of an event. Coronary CT angiography can show existing disease, including plaque that a calcium scan misses. In a Scottish substudy, scan findings changed who qualified for preventive medication in about one in three participants. Better targeting could prevent first attacks and spare some people unnecessary medication. The benefit depends on people taking effective treatment and on gains outweighing harms such as bleeding.

figures.caption: Estimated annual myocardial infarctions in the United States
figures.note: The 2026 update uses incidence data from 2005–2014.

statements.quote: It may be appropriate to perform CTA in selected asymptomatic high risk individuals
whether it lowers the number of people developing heart disease compared to those using the risk score.
statements.context: The sponsor describes comparing CT-guided treatment decisions with decisions guided by a cardiovascular risk score.

statements.quote: It is rarely appropriate to perform CTA in low or intermediate risk asymptomatic subjects.
statements.context: Section 4.3 of the expert consensus document addresses clinical use in asymptomatic people at low or intermediate risk.

statements.quote: Primary preventive treatment guided by CTCA reduces the risk of myocardial infarction and cardiovascular death
statements.context: The DANE-HEART registration states this as its primary hypothesis. The trial compares CT-guided prevention with care guided by the SCORE2 cardiovascular risk model.

completion.title: CT-guided prevention reduces first coronary events in asymptomatic adults in a randomized trial.
completion.criterion: Randomize at least 6,000 protocol-eligible asymptomatic Scottish adults aged 40–70 with at least one cardiovascular risk factor 1:1 to CT-guided or ASSIGN score-guided prevention. Show a lower risk of the first occurrence of coronary heart disease death or nonfatal myocardial infarction in the adjusted intention-to-treat analysis. Use Cox regression, with restricted mean survival time if hazards are nonproportional. The 5% design uses Lan–DeMets alpha spending with O’Brien–Fleming boundaries at 4, 5, 6 and 7 years after study start and permits longer follow-up if too few events accrue.
completion.set_by: University of Edinburgh and Lothian Health Board, SCOT-HEART 2 protocol version 5, dated 13 December 2023, sections 2.2 and 8.
completion.threshold_quote: The primary outcome will be coronary heart disease death or non-fatal myocardial infarction.
completion.basis: SCOT-HEART 2 recruited 6,139 participants. The sponsor reported ongoing follow-up on 17 September 2026. Bleeding, procedures and cost-effectiveness are secondary outcomes. FACTOR-64 enrolled 900 asymptomatic adults with diabetes. Over a mean 4.0 years, 28 participants assigned to CT screening and 34 assigned to usual care reached its composite of death, nonfatal infarction or unstable-angina admission (6.2% versus 7.6%, hazard ratio 0.80, 95% CI 0.49–1.32, P=0.38).

milestones.title: Deep-learning CT plaque volumes are validated against catheter ultrasound and an independent cohort.
milestones.criterion: For deep-learning models that quantify coronary plaque from CT, SCCT requires comparison with invasive reference imaging and testing in a cohort independent of training. Lin et al. (2022) compared plaque volumes with catheter-based intravascular ultrasound in 50 patients with 84 lesions, obtaining an intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.949 (95% CI 0.921–0.967). Their external validation cohort comprised 175 SCOT-HEART patients with 1,081 lesions. SCCT specifies these comparisons without a numerical agreement cutoff.
milestones.set_by: Society of Cardiovascular Computed Tomography, 2024 quantitative CCTA standards, requirements for deep-learning models.
milestones.threshold_quote: and to (ii) external validation in a fully independent cohort.

milestones.title: CT plaque volume predicts infarction in stable chest pain after adjustment for risk and stenosis (P<0.05).
milestones.criterion: In patients with stable chest pain, test whether higher total coronary plaque volume on CT is associated with subsequent fatal or nonfatal myocardial infarction. Use multivariable Cox regression adjusting for the ASSIGN clinical risk score and obstructive stenosis of at least 50%. Require a positive association at two-sided P<0.05. A volume cutoff estimated in the outcome cohort requires separate validation before clinical use.
milestones.set_by: Community convention for testing adjusted prognostic associations, applied in Lin et al. (2022), Statistical analysis.
milestones.threshold_quote: A two-sided p value of <0·05 indicated statistical significance.

milestones.title: At six months, ≥10 percentage points more adults in CT-guided care meet all four lifestyle targets.
milestones.criterion: Compare the proportions meeting all four targets at six months in the CT-guided and risk-score groups: BMI 18.5–25 kg/m², five fruit and vegetable servings daily plus oily fish twice weekly, nonsmoking, and at least 150 minutes of moderate or 75 minutes of vigorous aerobic activity weekly. The substudy used a 10-percentage-point absolute increase, from 5% to 15%, as its meaningful effect for sample-size planning. Test the between-group difference against zero at two-sided P<0.05.
milestones.set_by: University of Edinburgh, registered SCOT-HEART 2 IMPACT substudy NCT04156061, primary endpoint and published sample-size target.
milestones.threshold_quote: improved compliance of at least 1 in 10 participants (15% total).

milestones.title: Coronary plaque seen on CT is matched to plaque in human coronary artery specimens.
milestones.criterion: Image human coronary specimens with contrast-enhanced CT, match lesions to the same sites on gross examination and compare their CT appearance with the tissue classification on histology. Report detection against the specimen reference.
milestones.set_by: SCCT's diagnostic-accuracy reference standard, applied to human coronary specimens by Becker and colleagues.
milestones.threshold_quote: compared to an accepted reference, e.g. histology

milestones.title: Deep-learning CT plaque volumes are validated against intravascular ultrasound.
milestones.criterion: Compare plaque volumes estimated from coronary CT angiography by the model with intravascular ultrasound measurements of the same lesions and report agreement. SCCT specifies the reference method without a numerical agreement cutoff.
milestones.set_by: Society of Cardiovascular Computed Tomography, 2024 quantitative CCTA standards.

milestones.title: Deep-learning CT plaque measurements are validated in a fully independent cohort.
milestones.criterion: Apply the trained plaque-quantification model to a fully independent external cohort and assess its measurements against reference measurements in that cohort. SCCT specifies external validation without a numerical agreement cutoff.
milestones.set_by: Society of Cardiovascular Computed Tomography, 2024 quantitative CCTA standards.
milestones.threshold_quote: external validation in a fully independent cohort.

milestones.title: CT-detected coronary stenosis of ≥50% identifies higher infarction risk in asymptomatic adults.
milestones.criterion: In a prospective cohort aged at least 40 without symptoms or known ischemic heart disease, classify coronary CT angiograms blind to treatment and outcomes. Compare subsequent myocardial infarction in people with at least 50% luminal stenosis against those with no coronary atherosclerosis. The adjusted relative risk must exceed 1 with a 95% confidence interval excluding 1.
milestones.set_by: Copenhagen General Population Study, using the conventional coronary CT definition of obstructive disease and adjusted relative risks with 95% confidence intervals.

milestones.title: Six-month uptake among adults offered preventive medication is higher with CT guidance at P<0.05.
milestones.criterion: Within each SCOT-HEART 2 IMPACT arm, use participants recommended preventive drug treatment as the denominator and those starting the recommended treatment by six months as the numerator. Compare these proportions with a two-sided test at P<0.05. Eligibility for a recommendation depends on the assigned strategy, so this comparison describes uptake among those offered treatment.
milestones.set_by: SCOT-HEART 2 IMPACT investigators, published medication-uptake comparison and statistical analysis.
milestones.threshold_quote: A 2-sided P value <.05 was considered statistically significant.

not_found: No SCOT-HEART 2 primary coronary-event result was found in publication and registry searches through 14 November 2026.
The detailed group-sequential statistical analysis plan could not be located.
No common numerical net-benefit acceptance threshold or affordability ceiling for asymptomatic coronary CT screening was found in the society, USPSTF and trial documents searched.
